questions.prompt: Which statement about binary search is true?

options.text: It can be applied to any unsorted list.
It requires the list to be sorted in ascending order.
It always runs in O(n) time.
It uses extra space proportional to the input size.

questions.explanation: Binary search only works on a sorted list; it runs in O(log n) time and uses O(1) extra space iteratively.

questions.prompt: Given the sorted array [3,5,7,9,11,13,15] and a target value of 9, which index (0‑based) will the iterative binary search examine first?
questions.explanation: With low=0 and high=6, the first mid index is (0+6)//2 = 3, so index 3 is checked first.

questions.prompt: In an iterative binary search on a sorted array, which condition correctly determines whether the search loop should continue?
questions.explanation: The loop must run while low <= high so that every possible index, including the case where low equals high, is examined.

questions.prompt: Given the sorted array [2,4,6,8,10,12,14], a recursive binary search is used to find the target value 10. Which value is compared with the target during the second recursive call?
questions.explanation: The first call compares the middle element 8; the second recursive call searches indices 4‑6, whose middle is 12, so 12 is compared next.

questions.prompt: In a binary search on a sorted array of length 8, after comparing the target with the middle element at index 3, the algorithm determines that the target is smaller than the middle element. What will be the new high index for the next iteration?
questions.explanation: When the target is smaller, the algorithm sets high = mid - 1, so the new high index becomes 2.

questions.prompt: Consider a sorted array of 1023 distinct integers. When performing an iterative binary search for a target that is not present, what is the maximum number of element comparisons that will be performed before the algorithm terminates?
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the search interval each step, so the worst‑case number of comparisons is ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉; for n=1023 this equals 10.

questions.prompt: When a recursive binary search is executed on a sorted array of length 31 to locate a target that is present, what is the maximum possible depth of the recursion stack?
questions.explanation: Each recursive call halves the remaining segment; the deepest call occurs when the segment size reaches 1, requiring ceil(log2(31)) = 5 levels.

questions.prompt: A sorted array contains 15 distinct integers. An iterative binary search is used to locate a target value that is larger than every element in the array. Including the final check that causes the loop to terminate, how many times is the loop condition `low <= high` evaluated?
questions.explanation: The algorithm performs ⌈log₂(15+1)⌉ = 4 iterations; the loop condition is evaluated once before each iteration and once more after the last iteration, giving a total of 5 evaluations.
